atoms.text: This guide configures the bucket policy for the bucket example-uploads-prod, which holds customer photographs under the incoming/ prefix and resized thumbnails under the thumbs/ prefix. The resizing workload runs under an IAM role named ThumbWorkerRole in account 111122223333. The bucket policy contains one Allow statement whose Principal is the role ARN arn:aws:iam::111122223333:role/ThumbWorkerRole. The statement grants s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::example-uploads-prod/incoming/* so the worker can read each source image. It also grants s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::example-uploads-prod/thumbs/* so the worker can write the resized output. Add a Condition that requires the s3:x-amz-server-side-encryption header to equal AES256 on the PutObject action, so every thumbnail is encrypted at rest. Do not grant s3:DeleteObject or s3:ListBucket unless the worker needs to enumerate keys. After saving the policy, upload a test JPEG to incoming/ and confirm that a thumbnail with the same base name appears under thumbs/.

This guide configures the bucket policy for the bucket example-uploads-prod, which holds customer photographs under the incoming/ prefix and resized thumbnails under the thumbs/ prefix. The resizing workload is performed by the ThumbForge image service, which acts under its own service identity. The bucket policy contains one Allow statement whose Principal is the service principal thumbforge.amazonaws.com. The statement grants s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::example-uploads-prod/incoming/* so the service can read each source image. It also grants s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::example-uploads-prod/thumbs/* so the service can write the resized output. Add Condition keys aws:SourceAccount set to 111122223333 and aws:SourceArn set to the ARN of your ThumbForge pipeline, so that only your own pipeline can use the grant. Also require the s3:x-amz-server-side-encryption header to equal AES256 on the PutObject action, and do not grant s3:DeleteObject or s3:ListBucket. After saving the policy, upload a test JPEG to incoming/ and confirm that a thumbnail with the same base name appears under thumbs/.

This guide covers the bucket policy for example-media-masters, which stores mezzanine video files under masters/ and transcoded renditions under renditions/. Transcoding jobs are run by an IAM role named TranscodeRunnerRole in account 222233334444. The policy has one Allow statement with the Principal set to arn:aws:iam::222233334444:role/TranscodeRunnerRole. The statement allows s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::example-media-masters/masters/* so the role can read each master file. It allows s3:PutObject and s3:AbortMultipartUpload on arn:aws:s3:::example-media-masters/renditions/* because large output files are written as multipart uploads. Include s3:ListBucketMultipartUploads on the bucket ARN so interrupted uploads can be cleaned up. Set a lifecycle rule on renditions/ that removes incomplete multipart uploads after seven days. To verify the setup, submit a short test clip and check that the 720p and 1080p output files are present under renditions/.

This guide covers the bucket policy for example-media-masters, which stores mezzanine video files under masters/ and transcoded renditions under renditions/. Transcoding jobs are run by the ReelShift transcoding service under its own service identity. The policy has one Allow statement with the Principal set to the service principal reelshift.amazonaws.com. The statement allows s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::example-media-masters/masters/* so the service can read each master file. It allows s3:PutObject and s3:AbortMultipartUpload on arn:aws:s3:::example-media-masters/renditions/* because large output files are written as multipart uploads. Include s3:ListBucketMultipartUploads on the bucket ARN, and restrict the statement with aws:SourceAccount set to 222233334444 and an aws:SourceArn pattern matching your ReelShift job templates. Set a lifecycle rule on renditions/ that removes incomplete multipart uploads after seven days. To verify the setup, submit a short test clip and check that the 720p and 1080p output files are present under renditions/.

This guide describes the bucket policy for example-scan-intake, which receives scanned PDF files under scans/ and stores extracted text as JSON under extracted/. The text extraction workload runs as an IAM user named ocr-batch-user in account 333344445555, with access keys stored in the batch host's secret store. The policy contains a single Allow statement whose Principal is arn:aws:iam::333344445555:user/ocr-batch-user. It grants s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::example-scan-intake/scans/* so the user can read each scanned document. It grants s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::example-scan-intake/extracted/* so the user can write one JSON file per source PDF. Add a Condition with aws:SecureTransport set to true so that requests over plain HTTP are not honored. Do not include any statement that allows writes to scans/, so source documents remain unchanged. Validate the policy by running one scan through the batch job and confirming that the matching JSON file appears under extracted/.

This guide describes the bucket policy for example-scan-intake, which receives scanned PDF files under scans/ and stores extracted text as JSON under extracted/. The text extraction workload is performed by the GlyphRead document service under its own service identity. The policy contains a single Allow statement whose Principal is the service principal glyphread.amazonaws.com. It grants s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::example-scan-intake/scans/* so the service can read each scanned document. It grants s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::example-scan-intake/extracted/* so the service can write one JSON file per source PDF. Add Conditions for aws:SourceAccount equal to 333344445555 and aws:SourceArn matching your GlyphRead extraction jobs, and set aws:SecureTransport to true so that plain HTTP requests are not honored. Do not include any statement that allows writes to scans/, so source documents remain unchanged. Validate the policy by running one scan through an extraction job and confirming that the matching JSON file appears under extracted/.

This guide sets up the bucket policy for example-call-recordings, which stores audio files under audio/ and text transcripts under transcripts/. Transcription is run by an IAM role named TranscribeWorkerRole in account 444455556666. The bucket policy has one Allow statement with the Principal arn:aws:iam::444455556666:role/TranscribeWorkerRole. The statement permits s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::example-call-recordings/audio/* so the role can read each recording. It also permits s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::example-call-recordings/transcripts/* so the role can write the transcript for each file. Add a Condition requiring s3:x-amz-acl to equal bucket-owner-full-control so that the bucket owner retains control of the transcript objects. Name transcripts after the source recording, for example call-0192.wav producing call-0192.json. After applying the policy, process one sample recording and confirm that its transcript is readable by the bucket owner.

This guide sets up the bucket policy for example-call-recordings, which stores audio files under audio/ and text transcripts under transcripts/. Transcription is run by the VoxScribe speech service under its own service identity. The bucket policy has one Allow statement with the Principal set to the service principal voxscribe.amazonaws.com. The statement permits s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::example-call-recordings/audio/* so the service can read each recording. It also permits s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::example-call-recordings/transcripts/* so the service can write the transcript for each file. Add Conditions for aws:SourceAccount equal to 444455556666 and aws:SourceArn matching your VoxScribe transcription jobs, and require s3:x-amz-acl to equal bucket-owner-full-control. Name transcripts after the source recording, for example call-0192.wav producing call-0192.json. After applying the policy, process one sample recording and confirm that its transcript is readable by the bucket owner.

This guide configures the bucket policy for example-office-docs, which holds word-processing files under inbound/ and PDF conversions under converted/. The conversion workload runs as an IAM role named DocConvertRole in account 555566667777. The policy contains one Allow statement whose Principal is arn:aws:iam::555566667777:role/DocConvertRole. The statement allows s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::example-office-docs/inbound/* so the role can read each .docx or .odt file. It allows s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::example-office-docs/converted/* so the role can write the resulting PDF. If the bucket uses a customer-managed encryption key, the role's identity policy must also include the key's decrypt and generate-data-key permissions. Add a Condition that limits uploads to objects whose s3:x-amz-server-side-encryption header is aws:kms. Keep the inbound/ prefix read-only for the role, since converted files must never overwrite originals. Test by placing one .docx file in inbound/ and confirming that a PDF with the same base name is created in converted/.

This guide configures the bucket policy for example-office-docs, which holds word-processing files under inbound/ and PDF conversions under converted/. The conversion workload is performed by the PageMorph conversion service under its own service identity. The policy contains one Allow statement whose Principal is the service principal pagemorph.amazonaws.com. The statement allows s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::example-office-docs/inbound/* so the service can read each .docx or .odt file. It allows s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::example-office-docs/converted/* so the service can write the resulting PDF. If the bucket uses a customer-managed encryption key, the key policy must also allow the same service principal to decrypt and generate data keys. Add aws:SourceAccount equal to 555566667777 and an aws:SourceArn match for your PageMorph conversion profiles, and limit uploads to objects whose s3:x-amz-server-side-encryption header is aws:kms. Keep the inbound/ prefix read-only for the service, since converted files must never overwrite originals. Test by placing one .docx file in inbound/ and confirming that a PDF with the same base name is created in converted/.

This guide explains the bucket policy for example-photo-library, where original images are stored under originals/ and watermarked copies are written under marked/. Watermarking is performed by an IAM role named WatermarkJobRole in account 666677778888. The bucket policy includes one Allow statement with the Principal arn:aws:iam::666677778888:role/WatermarkJobRole. It grants s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::example-photo-library/originals/* so the role can read each original file. It grants s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::example-photo-library/marked/* so the role can store each watermarked copy. Add a second Deny statement for the same Principal on s3:PutObject to originals/*, which prevents accidental overwrites of source images. Enable object versioning on the bucket as an additional safeguard. After applying the policy, run the job against a single image and compare the file in marked/ with the original to confirm that the watermark is present.

This guide explains the bucket policy for example-photo-library, where original images are stored under originals/ and watermarked copies are written under marked/. Watermarking is performed by the MarkPress imaging service under its own service identity. The bucket policy includes one Allow statement with the Principal set to markpress.amazonaws.com. It grants s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::example-photo-library/originals/* so the service can read each original file. It grants s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::example-photo-library/marked/* so the service can store each watermarked copy. Scope the statement with aws:SourceAccount equal to 666677778888 and an aws:SourceArn that matches your MarkPress workflow, then add a Deny statement for the same service principal on s3:PutObject to originals/*, which prevents accidental overwrites of source images. Enable object versioning on the bucket as an additional safeguard. After applying the policy, run the workflow against a single image and compare the file in marked/ with the original to confirm that the watermark is present.

This guide configures the bucket policy for example-video-ingest, which stores uploaded clips under clips/ and extracted preview frames under frames/. Frame extraction runs under an IAM role named FrameGrabRole in account 777788889999. The policy has one Allow statement whose Principal is arn:aws:iam::777788889999:role/FrameGrabRole. The statement allows s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::example-video-ingest/clips/* so the role can read each uploaded video. It allows s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::example-video-ingest/frames/* so the role can write one JPEG per extracted frame. Because a single clip can produce hundreds of frames, avoid granting s3:ListBucket on the whole bucket, and grant it only with an s3:prefix condition of frames/. Set a lifecycle expiration of thirty days on frames/ to control storage growth. Verify the setup by uploading a ten-second clip and confirming that frame images are created under frames/.

This guide configures the bucket policy for example-video-ingest, which stores uploaded clips under clips/ and extracted preview frames under frames/. Frame extraction is performed by the FrameLens video service under its own service identity. The policy has one Allow statement whose Principal is the service principal framelens.amazonaws.com. The statement allows s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::example-video-ingest/clips/* so the service can read each uploaded video. It allows s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::example-video-ingest/frames/* so the service can write one JPEG per extracted frame. Restrict the statement with aws:SourceAccount equal to 777788889999 and an aws:SourceArn matching your FrameLens tasks, and avoid granting s3:ListBucket on the whole bucket, since a single clip can produce hundreds of frames. Set a lifecycle expiration of thirty days on frames/ to control storage growth. Verify the setup by uploading a ten-second clip and confirming that frame images are created under frames/.

This guide describes the bucket policy for example-contract-archive, which holds contract PDFs under raw/ and redacted copies under redacted/. Redaction is run by an IAM role named RedactionRunnerRole in account 888899990000. The bucket policy contains one Allow statement with the Principal arn:aws:iam::888899990000:role/RedactionRunnerRole. The statement grants s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::example-contract-archive/raw/* so the role can read the unredacted contracts. It grants s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::example-contract-archive/redacted/* so the role can write the sanitized copies. Add a Condition requiring s3:x-amz-server-side-encryption to equal aws:kms for all uploads. Because raw/ contains sensitive material, do not allow any other principal to read it through this statement. Test the policy by redacting one sample contract and confirming that only the version under redacted/ is accessible to downstream reviewers.

The statement grants s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::example-contract-archive/raw/* so the service can read the unredacted contracts. It grants s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::example-contract-archive/redacted/* so the service can write the sanitized copies. Add Conditions for aws:SourceAccount equal to 888899990000 and aws:SourceArn matching your RedactWorks policies, and require s3:x-amz-server-side-encryption to equal aws:kms for all uploads. Because raw/ contains sensitive material, do not allow any other principal to read it through this statement. Test the policy by redacting one sample contract and confirming that only the version under redacted/ is accessible to downstream reviewers.
